findings.anchor: /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/imas-ambix/docs/plans/jt60sa-geometry-and-signal-figures.html:80 (owner: imas_ambix/data/signal_map.py:117 SignalRule.static_scale, applied through imas_ambix/data/virtual_zarr.py:75 VirtualArray.__getitem__)
findings.reason: reading values through the bound VirtualArray (whose scale is the map's) and using read_channel only for the time base the engine lacks makes the map the single owner of the conversion, so a later unit_factor or COCOS bound into a map is drawn correctly instead of silently dropped.
findings.text: §3 draws the bound coil-current and plasma-current channels by reading raw values through the new read_channel and multiplying by the map's channel_factor alone, while the map that owns that conversion reduces it to unit_factor * channel_factor * convention_factor (SignalRule.static_scale) and the engine path already applies it in VirtualArray.__getitem__; the plan even opens the bound VirtualArray to take the target unit from its attrs but takes the values elsewhere, so the conversion is re-implemented outside its owner in a partial form that happens to be numerically exact only because every JT-60SA pf_active rule currently carries unit_factor 1.0 and no COCOS transformation (imas_ambix/data/maps/jt-60sa/pf_active.json)

duplicate_owner-1.reason: plan v45 §3 takes each bound channel's values from VirtualZarrView, whose VirtualArray applies the map's whole conversion (channel_factor and SignalRule.static_scale), never scaling raw values; this matches the landed run, which already drew bound values through VirtualZarrView

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds one data function (§3 read_channel) and one test (§2b), each hiding a small amount of work behind a single name; nothing is spread across a family of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-derives the map-owned source-to-target conversion by applying only channel_factor while reading values raw, rather than letting the bound VirtualArray apply the map's full scale.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 adds the single public name read_channel and states in its own text that it "retires nothing" and is "the read counterpart nothing there provides", §4 states "it retires nothing; it is the one public addition, reusing the type the 3D path already exports", and §2b adds no public name — so every section that touches a family accounts for it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the two codebases it names: §2/§4 rebuild no imas-ink machinery (they call extract_geometry/geometry_figure_mpl, and §4 correctly records that imas-ink's shipped geometry-figure-vessel-units plan now owns the vessel reading), and §3's read_channel has no predecessor in imas_ambix/data/eddb.py or elsewhere (grep for a cache reader returns nothing); the one unshipped dependency — imas-ink's trace-figure-display-resolution (draft v1, no sections) — is declared in plan-section-depends-on, so the search is accounted for.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3 states why the existing value path cannot serve: VirtualZarrView/ZarrTransformEngine return values with no time base (virtual_zarr.py:75-76 returns only the transformed slice), and read_channel is the raw read counterpart eddb.py lacks; the wrapper is justified rather than parallel.
